newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest restaurant faces fine over $6,000 dinner.
newsitem.headline: Budapest restaurant faces fine over $6,000 dinner.

text.p: A Budapest restaurant which charged two Danish tourists and two women companions more than $6,000 for dinner and drinks may be fined up to 30,000 forints ($176), city officials said on Tuesday.

Consumer protection authorities said they had begun a legal proceeding against the Dreher Halaszcsarda after Preben Olsen lodged a complaint at a tourist office, saying he had been charged more than 1 million forints, newspapers said.
The newspapers said the restaurant had a policy of multiplying listed prices by a factor of 10 after 7 p.m.
"These are our night prices," Imre Lehoczky, the restaurant's business manager, told the daily Nepszabadsag newspaper. "We charge what the market will bear."
The legal proceeding against the restaurant's owner seeks a fine of up to 30,000 forints, the maximum allowed by law, one official source said.
The U.S. Embassy in Budapest last week warned about overpricing and strongarm tactics employed in some Budapest cafes and nightclubs, although the Halaszcsarda was not among them.
